prompt.text: Many cities are creating small gardens on the roofs of public buildings. These green spaces abs[orb] rainwater and prov[ide] a home for insects. They also red[uce] the amount of heat that enters the building. However, a rooftop garden req[uires] careful planning. Engineers must make sure the roof can sup[port] the weight of soil and water.

questions.feedback: The complete words are absorb, provide, reduce, requires and support. Use both grammar and context to reconstruct the missing letters.

prompt.title: Campus bicycle workshop
prompt.passage:
From: Campus Transport Office
Subject: Bicycle repairs this Friday

Our free bicycle workshop will move from the courtyard to Room 104 because rain is expected. Volunteers can fix flat tires and adjust brakes. Please reserve a time online by Thursday evening. Students without a reservation may join the waiting list at the door.
prompt.question: What should a student do to guarantee a time at the workshop?
options: Join the waiting list on Friday
Reserve a time before Friday
Bring a bicycle to the courtyard
Contact a volunteer after the workshop

questions.feedback: The email asks students to reserve online by Thursday evening. The waiting list does not guarantee a place.

prompt.title: The role of urban wetlands
prompt.passage:
Urban wetlands were once considered obstacles to construction. Many were drained so that roads and buildings could occupy the land. More recently, researchers have shown that these areas provide valuable services to cities. Their plants and soils absorb rainfall, slowing the movement of water into drainage systems during storms.

Wetlands also improve water quality. As water moves slowly through vegetation, suspended particles settle. Microorganisms in the soil can transform some pollutants into less harmful substances. These processes require time, which is why a wetland cannot always be replaced by a small decorative pond.

Restoring wetlands, however, presents a planning challenge. Land is expensive, and residents may prefer immediate uses such as parking or housing. Supporters of restoration therefore emphasize the long-term costs that wetlands can prevent, including flood damage and the construction of larger drainage systems.
prompt.question: Why does the author mention a small decorative pond?
options: To propose a cheaper alternative to wetland restoration
To explain that all ponds remove the same pollutants
To illustrate why the functions of a wetland are not easily reproduced
To argue that vegetation interferes with water treatment

questions.feedback: The comparison emphasizes that the slow processes performed by a wetland need sufficient space and time.

prompt.transcript: Could you tell me where I can return these library books?
prompt.question: Select the best response.

I read that book last summer.

prompt.transcript: Attention students. The east entrance to the science building will be closed on Monday while new doors are installed. Please use the north entrance next to the bus stop. The building's classrooms and laboratories will remain open as usual. Deliveries should be taken to the loading area behind the building. We expect the east entrance to reopen on Tuesday morning.
prompt.question: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To cancel Monday's science classes
To explain a temporary change in building access
To announce a new bus stop
To ask students to help install new doors

prompt.transcript: Today I want to discuss why some seeds remain inactive for years. A seed needs more than water to begin growing. It may also need a particular temperature or a period of exposure to cold. These requirements prevent it from growing at an unfavorable time. Consider a plant that produces seeds in autumn. If every seed began growing during a brief warm spell, the young plants could die when winter arrived. A requirement for several weeks of cold helps the seeds wait until spring. This delay is not a failure to grow. It is a survival strategy that links growth to environmental conditions.
prompt.context: A biology instructor is explaining seed dormancy.
prompt.question: According to the instructor, what is an advantage of a seed's need for prolonged cold?
options: It allows the plant to produce seeds in winter.
It reduces the amount of water a seed needs.
It helps prevent growth during an unsuitable season.
It makes young plants resistant to every temperature.

questions.feedback: The cold requirement prevents germination during a temporary warm spell before winter.

prompt.question: Why did you choose the afternoon workshop?

questions.feedback: Because it fit my schedule better. The clause begins with because, followed by the subject and past-tense verb.

prompt.scenario: You are organizing a student photography exhibition. The university events coordinator has offered you a room, but it is too small for the number of visitors you expect. Write an email to the coordinator, Ms. Lee.
requiredPoints: Thank her for offering the room.
Explain why you need a larger space.
Suggest an alternative and ask whether it is available.

questions.feedback: Address all three points, use a suitable greeting and closing, and make a clear, polite request.

prompt.professorPost: Professor Morgan: Some universities require students to complete a community service project before graduating. Others believe students should decide for themselves how to use their time outside class. Should community service be a graduation requirement? Explain your position and contribute a new idea to the discussion.

studentReplies.author: Aisha
studentReplies.text: A requirement can introduce students to problems they would not otherwise notice. Working with a local organization also gives them practical experience.

studentReplies.author: Daniel
studentReplies.text: Students who work long hours may not have time for an additional requirement. Universities should encourage volunteering without making it compulsory.

questions.feedback: State your position, develop it with relevant detail, and respond to the discussion without copying the other students' wording.
